chunks: Everything in it that is from ʿAbd Allah ibn Miskan, I have transmitted from my father and from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-ʿAttar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Miskan.
And he was a Kufan, one of the mawali of ʿAnazah, and it is also said that he was one of the mawali of ʿIjl.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: A supplicatory honorific meaning: may Allah be pleased with them both.
key_terms.كُوفِيٌّ: A native or resident of Kufah.
key_terms.مَوَالِي عَنَزَةَ: Affiliated clients or freedmen connected to the tribe of ʿAnazah.
key_terms.مَوَالِي عِجْلٍ: Affiliated clients or freedmen connected to the tribe of ʿIjl.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to ʿAbd Allah ibn Miskan in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage gives the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from ʿAbd Allah ibn Miskan. It also briefly identifies him as a Kufan and notes differing reports about the tribe to which his walaʾ affiliation was connected.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abdullah ibn Miskan has been transmitted by me from my father and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah (swt) be pleased with them both - from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan.
He was a Kufan and a freed servant (mawla) of the tribe of Anzah, and it is also said that he was a freed servant of the tribe of Ujl.
